standard.title: Develop questions to guide investigations
standard.description: develop questions to guide investigations about people, events, places and issues
standard.prior_knowledge: From Y3 (AC9HS3S01): Students developed location, consequence and ethical questions using inquiring question types.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students develop questions to guide investigations about people, events, places and issues, including discipline-specific and 'How do we know?' questions.

nodes.label: Discipline-specific inquiry questions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can develop questions that address disciplinary concepts from history, geography and civics, including 'What was the cause?', 'What are the characteristics of this place?' and 'How can we manage resources sustainably?'
nodes.minimum_width: Develop at least three inquiry questions using disciplinary question types from at least two different HASS disciplines.
nodes.typical_width: Develop questions addressing: cause ('What was the cause?'), significance ('Why was this event significant?'), change ('How did daily life change?'), place ('What are the characteristics of this place?'), sustainability ('How can we manage resources sustainably?'), rules ('What rules are used by...?') and evidence ('How do we know?').
wider: Evaluate whether a set of inquiry questions adequately covers all disciplinary perspectives on a topic
Develop questions that link historical, geographical and civic aspects of the same issue (e.g. colonisation affects history, geography and civic rights)

response_modes.reason: Discipline-specific questions are the most sophisticated question type at Year 4 — practise across multiple disciplines before expecting fluent integration.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Multi-disciplinary question development is the highest-order inquiry skill in HASS — students who can interrogate a topic from history, geography AND civics angles simultaneously demonstrate deep inquiry capability.
success_criteria: Develops at least three questions from at least two HASS disciplines
At least one question targets disciplinary evidence ('How do we know?')
